title: Family and Friends
subtitle: Family occasions and friendships in Elmstead

parts.title: Family notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: SUNDAY LUNCH: Change of plan! Lunch at Gran’s is now at 2 p.m. instead of 1 p.m., because Grandad’s train is late. Please bring a dessert. Gran will cook everything else.
SURPRISE PARTY: Dad’s 60th is on Saturday, and it’s a secret! Please arrive by 4 p.m. and park round the corner so that he doesn’t see the cars.
SISTER: Mum’s train gets in at 5.40, not 4.40. I’m at work until six, so can you meet her at the station? I’ll make dinner when we get home.

ELMSTEAD SCHOOL REUNION: Come and meet old classmates on Friday 14 June at 7 p.m. in the school hall. Please reply by 1 June so that we can order the right amount of food. Bring an old photo if you have one.
BABYSITTER AVAILABLE: Local student, first-aid trained, with experience of children aged two to ten. Evenings and weekends, £10 an hour. Ask at number 14.

questions.prompt: What has changed about Sunday’s lunch?
options: It will now take place in a restaurant.
It has been cancelled because of the train.
It will start later than planned.
questions.explanation: Lunch is now at 2 p.m. instead of 1 p.m., so it starts later than planned.

questions.prompt: Why should guests park round the corner?
options: So that Dad does not notice them arriving.
There is not enough space outside his house.
The road in front of the house will be closed.
questions.explanation: The party is a surprise, so cars must be out of sight so that Dad does not see them.

questions.prompt: What does the sister want the reader to do?
options: Cook dinner for the whole family at home.
Meet their mother at the train station.
Change the time of their mother’s train ticket.
questions.explanation: The sister is at work until six, so she asks the reader to meet Mum at the station.

questions.prompt: What must guests do before 1 June?
options: Send an old photo to the school by post.
Tell the organisers that they will be coming.
Pay in advance for their meal at the reunion.
questions.explanation: Guests must reply by 1 June so that the organisers can order food; the old photo is optional and is brought on the day.

questions.prompt: What is being offered on the sign?
options: Child care in the evenings and at weekends
Private lessons for young children at home
A cleaning service for houses and flats
questions.explanation: The sign advertises a babysitter for evenings and weekends.

parts.title: Choosing a present for a relative or friend
parts.instructions: Read what each person is looking for. Match each person to the best gift or activity. There are three extra ideas.

people.text: Helga’s grandfather loves history and stories, but his eyesight is getting worse, so he cannot read small print any more.
Bartosz’s sister has just had a baby. He wants a gift for the baby’s first shoes, cards and other small things to keep.
Ece would like to do something fun with her fifteen-year-old cousin and two of his friends.
Satoshi is looking for a present for his aunt, who spends every weekend outside in her garden.
Fiona’s best friend is moving to another country. She wants to give her something that will remind her of home.

texts.title: Pizza-making evening
texts.text: Learn to make pizza from scratch with a chef and eat what you cook. Adults only. Booking is needed at least a week ahead.

texts.title: Weekend spa break
texts.text: Two nights in a quiet hotel with a swimming pool and a spa. Suitable for adults who want to relax.

texts.title: Custom photo book
texts.text: A gift for a friend who lives far away: upload your favourite pictures and we will print them in a hardback book with a title of your choice. Ready in five days.

texts.title: Baby memory box
texts.text: A soft cloth box for a baby’s first shoes, cards and hospital bracelet. It lasts for many years and can be given from the day of the birth.

texts.title: Karaoke party for six

texts.title: Garden centre voucher
texts.text: Give a voucher to spend on plants, tools and pots at any of our garden centres. It stays valid for a whole year.

texts.title: Escape room game
texts.text: Solve puzzles together in a locked room and try to get out in sixty minutes. For groups of two to six people aged twelve and over.

texts.title: Audiobook subscription
texts.text: Listen to hundreds of stories and history books on any phone or radio, with no screen and no small print. Three months for the price of two.

questions.prompt: Helga
questions.explanation: Helga’s grandfather loves stories and history but cannot read small print; audiobooks need no screen and no reading.

questions.prompt: Bartosz
questions.explanation: Bartosz wants something to keep the baby’s first shoes and cards in; the memory box is made for exactly that and can be given from birth.

questions.prompt: Ece
questions.explanation: Ece wants a fun activity for her cousin and two friends; the escape room is for groups of two to six aged twelve and over.

questions.prompt: Satoshi
questions.explanation: Satoshi’s aunt spends her weekends in the garden; a garden centre voucher can be spent on plants, tools and pots.

questions.prompt: Fiona
questions.explanation: Fiona wants a reminder of home for a friend abroad; a photo book for a friend who lives far away is made from the pictures you choose.

parts.title: A big family reunion
parts.instructions: Read the text and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Every five years, my mother’s family holds a reunion, and this summer it was our turn to organise it. My grandmother is eighty-two and has seven children, so there were forty-three of us in the end, from babies to great-uncles. It took six months of planning, and my job was to put together a slideshow of old family photos. I spent weeks asking relatives to send me pictures, and some of them were very funny. There was one of my dad in the 1990s with hair down to his shoulders.

On the day, things did not go quite as planned. Half the guests arrived an hour early, while we were still putting up tables, so my aunts ended up carrying chairs in their best clothes. Nobody minded, though. By the time the food came, the hall was loud with laughter.

I was nervous about meeting some of my cousins, because I had not seen them since I was a child. I thought we would have nothing to talk about. It turned out that we all liked the same bands and even supported the same football team, and we talked until it got dark.

The slideshow was the biggest success, and my grandmother cried when she saw her wedding photo. Afterwards, she asked if we could do it again next year instead of waiting five years. We all agreed that was too soon, but I have already started a folder on my laptop for the next reunion.

questions.prompt: Why was the writer’s family responsible for this year’s reunion?
options: It was their turn to organise it.
Their grandmother was too old to do it.
His grandmother had chosen them for the job.
They have the biggest house in the family.
questions.explanation: The reunion is held every five years, and this summer “it was our turn to organise it”.

questions.prompt: What was the writer’s task?
options: To send invitations to all the relatives.
To book the hall and order the food.
To collect old pictures and show them.
questions.explanation: His job was to put together a slideshow of old family photos, which meant asking relatives for pictures.

questions.prompt: What went wrong on the day?
options: Several guests forgot that the reunion was on.
Many people arrived before the family was ready.
There were not enough chairs for everybody there.
The food arrived much later than planned.
questions.explanation: Half the guests arrived an hour early, while the family was still putting up tables.

questions.prompt: How did he feel about his cousins after meeting them?
options: Worried that they would not remember him at all.
Disappointed that they lived so far away from him.
Pleased to find that they shared his tastes.
Surprised to find that they were so different.
questions.explanation: They liked the same bands and supported the same football team, so he found they had a lot in common.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say at the end?
options: He has already begun to prepare the next one.
A reunion every year would be much better for all.
His grandmother wants to move to a smaller house.
The slideshow was far too long for the guests.
questions.explanation: He says he has already started a folder on his laptop for the next reunion.

parts.title: Friends since the age of four
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Eimear and Anika have known each other since they were four, when they sat next to each other on their first day at primary school. [1] Nineteen years later, they still speak almost every day.

As children, they lived on the same street in Elmstead, so they walked to school together every morning. [2] Their parents say the two girls hardly ever argued, and when they did, they made up within an hour.

Things changed when Eimear moved to a city far away to study. [3] Anika, on the other hand, stayed in Elmstead to train as a nurse. They were afraid that the distance would end their friendship. [4] “We wrote long emails and had a video call every Sunday evening,” says Eimear.

Next month, Anika will stand next to Eimear at her wedding. [5] “Good friends do not need to see each other all the time,” says Anika, “but they never forget each other’s birthdays.”
sentences: It was the beginning of a friendship that has never stopped.
Neither of them has ever enjoyed travelling by plane.
It was the first time that they had lived in different cities.
Instead, they found new ways to stay in touch.
At secondary school, they joined the same choir and the same netball team.
Both of them agree that such a long friendship has taught them something important.
He sent them a card every year on their birthday.
Nobody in either family had ever lived abroad.

gaps.explanation: “It” refers to the first day at school, and “the beginning of a friendship” leads to “Nineteen years later, they still speak almost every day”.
After the primary-school years, “At secondary school” continues the history; it leads to what their parents say about the two girls.
“The first time that they had lived in different cities” follows Eimear’s move and prepares “Anika, on the other hand, stayed in Elmstead”.
“Instead” contrasts with the fear that distance would end the friendship, and the quotation explains how they stayed in touch.
The sentence about what the friendship has taught them leads into Anika’s opinion about good friends. Sentence B is about flying and fits no gap.

parts.title: A cousin’s wedding
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: My cousin got married last Saturday, and the whole family [1] at the church. The bride arrived [2] a vintage car, wearing a long white dress. After the ceremony, we all [3] photographs outside while the bells rang. At the reception, the bride’s father made a very funny [4], and then everyone started to dance. I danced so much that my feet [5]. It was the [6] day of the year for our family.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: People gather at a place when they come together there; “gathered at the church” is correct.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: You arrive “in a car”; “by car” needs no article, so “by a vintage car” is wrong.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: We “take photographs”; the other verbs do not go with photographs.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: At a wedding, the bride’s father makes a speech.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: After lots of dancing, her feet hurt.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: After “the”, a superlative is needed: “the happiest day of the year”.

parts.title: A letter to an old friend
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Nigel,
I was so happy to get your letter last week. It is hard to believe that we have not seen each other [1] ten years! I often think [2] the summers we spent on my grandmother’s farm. Do you remember [3] we used to build a tree house in the old apple tree? I still have the photo that your mother took [4] us. I have moved to a small town by the sea, and there is a spare bedroom in my flat. Please come and stay [5] you are free in the summer. Write back soon and tell [6] all your news!
With love,
Helga

gaps.explanation: “For ten years” shows the length of time since they last met.
We “think of” or “think about” something we remember.
“Do you remember how we used to build…” introduces a memory.
We say “a photo of us”: the photo shows them.
“If you are free” makes the invitation depend on his time.

parts.title: Short conversations with family and friends
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What shall we do for Mum’s birthday? I was going to book that Italian restaurant.

turns.speaker: sharni
turns.text: She doesn’t like restaurants these days. She says they’re too noisy. And a day at the seaside is too much, it’s two hours away and she gets tired in the car.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: So what do you suggest?

turns.speaker: sharni
turns.text: Remember the park near her house, the one with the lake? She loves it there. We could have a picnic there, outdoors, with sandwiches and her favourite lemon cake, and sit on a blanket under the big tree. If it’s sunny, of course.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: That sounds perfect. I’ll make the cake myself.

turns.speaker: sharni
turns.text: Great. I’ll bring the sandwiches and some lemonade.

question.prompt: What do they plan for their mother’s birthday?
question.explanation: Their mother finds restaurants noisy and the seaside is too far, so they will take sandwiches and cake to the park by the lake.

turns.speaker: julian
turns.text: Hi Elif, it’s Julian. About my cousin who is coming on Friday. I thought she could sleep in the spare room, but it’s full of boxes and the floor is still wet from the paint, so that’s no good. You said there’s a hotel nearby, and she’d like that, but she’s a student and doesn’t have much money. So here’s my idea. We put the sofa bed in the living room. It’s very comfortable, and she can watch television late. Please find clean sheets for it. I’ll move the table tomorrow. Thanks, see you tonight.

question.explanation: The spare room is full of boxes and a hotel is too expensive for a student, so the cousin will sleep on the sofa bed in the living room.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: Hi Youssef, it’s Brigid. Thanks for offering to help with Mum’s dinner on Sunday. Dinner is at eight, and the guests are arriving at half past seven. I know you asked to come at seven thirty because you work until late on Sundays, but I need you earlier, to chop the vegetables and put the plates on the table. Please come at six thirty. I will make you a coffee when you arrive. If it’s impossible, just send me a text. Otherwise I’ll see you then.

question.explanation: Guests come at half past seven and dinner is at eight, but she needs him earlier to help with the cooking, so he should arrive at half past six.

turns.speaker: dai
turns.text: Whitney, where are you? Your flight should be here by now.

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: Hi Dai. We landed an hour ago, but the bags are very slow. I’m still waiting.

turns.speaker: dai
turns.text: Shall I drive to the airport right now? I can be there in twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: Please don’t. It will be at least another hour before I’m out. I’ll send you a text when I have my suitcase and I’m ready to go.

turns.speaker: dai
turns.text: Okay. And do you want me to book you another flight for next week?

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: No, no. The airline already gave me a seat for the return.

turns.speaker: dai
turns.text: Fine. I’ll sit here with my coffee and wait for your text.

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: Thanks. You’re a star.

options: Drive to the airport right now
Wait for her to send a text
question.explanation: He offers to drive now and to book another flight, but she says no to both; she will message him when she has her bag, so he waits for her text.

turns.speaker: jodie
turns.text: Look at this old photo from the beach. Our father is wearing that silly big hat.

turns.speaker: radek
turns.text: No, our father has his straw hat on, and he’s holding the umbrella. The big hat is on somebody else.

turns.speaker: jodie
turns.text: Is it me? I remember a hat like that.

turns.speaker: radek
turns.text: Jodie, you had a little pink one, with the flower. I was wearing Gran’s hat. I thought it was hilarious.

turns.speaker: jodie
turns.text: Of course! Now I can see it. Your face is under the brim, and you look about six.

turns.speaker: radek
turns.text: I was seven, actually. I wore it all afternoon.

turns.speaker: jodie
turns.text: We should put this photo on the wall.

question.prompt: Who is wearing a big hat in the photo?
question.explanation: Their father has a smaller straw hat and Jodie’s hat was a little pink one; the big one was Gran’s hat, which Radek wore.

turns.speaker: skye
turns.text: Osian, where were you? It’s nearly midnight.

turns.speaker: osian
turns.text: Sorry, I missed the bus, but I’m only ten minutes late.

turns.speaker: skye
turns.text: It isn’t that. You came back late yesterday too, and I was fine with it. I’m annoyed about my sister’s present. You said you would pick it up from the shop on your way home.

turns.speaker: osian
turns.text: Oh no! I completely forgot.

turns.speaker: skye
turns.text: The shop is closed now, and her party is tomorrow. And somebody ate my food, a whole plate of lasagne, but I know that was Dad.

turns.speaker: osian
turns.text: I’m really sorry. I’ll go first thing in the morning.

options: He forgot to do something he promised
He came home very late at night again
He ate some of the food that was hers
question.explanation: She says being late is not the problem and she blames her father for the lasagne; she is annoyed because Osian forgot to collect the present that he promised.

turns.speaker: aylin
turns.text: Hi Bao, it’s Aylin. Thank you so much for the lovely present! I was sure that you would buy me a book, because I’m always reading, and when I saw the flowers on the table I thought they were from you. But they were from my aunt. Your gift is much better. It’s the softest scarf I’ve ever owned, and the colour goes perfectly with my winter coat. I wore it all day today. Anyway, I hope you have a good weekend. Call me soon!

question.prompt: What did the man give the woman?
question.explanation: She expected a book and the flowers were from her aunt; Bao gave her a soft scarf.

parts.title: Feelings and everyday problems
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: nabil
turns.text: Did you see what I did to your phone? I changed the language to Japanese!

turns.speaker: ploy
turns.text: Very funny. It took me an hour to change it back.

turns.speaker: nabil
turns.text: Are you going to tell our parents?

turns.speaker: ploy
turns.text: No, I won’t bother them. And I don’t need a new phone, it works fine. But tomorrow you’ll find your laptop screen upside down and everything in Greek.

turns.speaker: nabil
turns.text: You wouldn’t dare.

turns.speaker: ploy
turns.text: Wait and see. I’m a very patient person.

question.prompt: What is Ploy going to do?
question.explanation: She will not tell her parents and does not need a new phone, but she plans to play a trick on his laptop in return.

turns.speaker: abena
turns.text: How are you feeling about the interview, Fintan? You look so confident in that suit.

turns.speaker: fintan
turns.text: Looks are deceiving. Honestly, my stomach hurts. I’ve practised the answers all week and I still think I’ll forget them.

turns.speaker: abena
turns.text: You’ll be fine. You know the job well.

turns.speaker: fintan
turns.text: I’m not angry about the job, I left my old one happily. I just can’t stop thinking about tomorrow at ten o’clock. I can’t eat anything.

turns.speaker: abena
turns.text: Try to sleep early tonight. Then it will go well.

turns.speaker: fintan
turns.text: I’ll try.

question.explanation: She says he looks confident, but he says his stomach hurts and he cannot stop thinking about tomorrow, so he is nervous.

turns.speaker: roisin
turns.text: I miss my old friend Kara. She moved to Canada and we haven’t talked for a year.

turns.speaker: nnamdi
turns.text: Why don’t you search for her online? Most people have a profile.

turns.speaker: roisin
turns.text: I could write her a long letter, but she has probably moved house again.

turns.speaker: nnamdi
turns.text: A letter takes weeks to arrive. And visiting Canada is expensive. Just look her up, then send a short message.

turns.speaker: roisin
turns.text: Good idea. I’ll try tonight.

turns.speaker: nnamdi
turns.text: Tell me what happens.

options: Visiting her in her new country
question.explanation: He thinks a letter takes too long and a visit costs too much; he says she should search for Kara online and send her a message.

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: I want to make Gran’s apple cake for Sunday, but I can’t find the recipe.

turns.speaker: osian
turns.text: Is it in the old recipe book?

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: The book is here on the shelf, I checked. Gran wasn’t a person who wrote things down. She cooked by feel.

turns.speaker: osian
turns.text: Didn’t Mum say it had too much sugar?

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: Maybe, but that’s not the issue. I’ll ask Aunt Rosa, she watched Gran bake for years.

turns.speaker: osian
turns.text: Good luck.

turns.speaker: whitney
turns.text: Thanks. I’ll write it down this time.

question.prompt: What is the problem with the recipe?
options: It has too much sugar in it.
The recipe book has been lost.
question.explanation: The book is on the shelf and the sugar is not the issue; Gran never wrote the recipe down, she cooked by feel.

turns.speaker: bao
turns.text: Your friend Mira is moving to Bristol, isn’t she? You must be happy for her.

turns.speaker: elif
turns.text: Of course. The new job is a big step, and visiting her will be fun, I’m sure.

turns.speaker: bao
turns.text: Is she going soon?

turns.speaker: elif
turns.text: Next month. Everyone says it’s good for her, but I keep thinking about our Saturday coffees. I’ll miss her so much.

turns.speaker: bao
turns.text: Are you relieved that it’s finally decided?

turns.speaker: elif
turns.text: Not really. The waiting wasn’t hard. It’s the goodbye that I’m afraid of.

question.prompt: How does Elif feel about her friend's move?
options: Sad that she will miss her
question.explanation: She says the job is a good step and visiting will be fun, but she keeps thinking about their Saturday coffees and is afraid of the goodbye, so she is sad.

turns.speaker: radek
turns.text: Dad told his joke about the penguin again at lunch.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: The same one! It’s so old. He has told it for twenty years.

turns.speaker: radek
turns.text: I know all the words. And yet I laughed, it’s still funny.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: Me too. It isn’t new, it isn’t difficult, and it isn’t rude. It’s just his face when he tells it, and he always forgets the end.

turns.speaker: radek
turns.text: We’ll be telling it to our kids.

turns.speaker: brigid
turns.text: And they’ll laugh too.

question.prompt: What do they say about their father's joke?
options: It is old but still funny to them.
It is new and hard to understand fully.
It is rude and not very funny at all.
question.explanation: They know the joke by heart after twenty years, it is not rude or difficult, and they still laugh because of how he tells it.

parts.title: A speech at a golden wedding
parts.instructions: Listen to the speech and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good evening, everyone, and welcome. I’m Dustin, the oldest of Gran and Grandad’s eight grandkids, and I have the pleasure of saying a few words tonight. Fifty years ago this month, Gran and Grandad got married. They wanted to marry in May, but the church was full, so the wedding was in June. They had met three years earlier, on a bus. Grandad likes to say it was a train, but Gran says it was a bus, the number twelve, and she is always right. After the wedding, they didn’t have much money. Their first home was a small flat above a bakery. Every morning they woke up to the smell of fresh bread, which Gran says was the best alarm clock in the world. Next door there was a butcher’s, and Grandad still says he preferred the smell of that, but nobody believes him. Now, Grandad’s job. For thirty years he was a driver on those same city routes, and he knew every street and every passenger. People still stop him in the supermarket to say hello. Gran, meanwhile, taught music at the primary school. She wanted to teach art, but the school needed a music teacher, and she learned to love it. Half of this room had a lesson with her! And she can still play the piano better than any of us. People always ask them the secret of their long marriage. Grandad usually says, never eat fish on Fridays. But Gran has a serious answer. She says, never go to bed angry. If you argue, you talk about it before you sleep, even if it takes until three o’clock. So please, everyone, raise your glasses to Gran and Grandad!

gaps.prompt: They got married fifty years ago, in the month of ___
gaps.explanation: They wanted May but the church was full, so the wedding was in June.
Grandad says it was a train, but Gran says it was a bus, number twelve.

gaps.prompt: Their first home was a small flat above a ___
gaps.explanation: The flat was above a bakery; the butcher’s was next door.

gaps.prompt: For thirty years Grandad worked as a bus ___
gaps.explanation: He was a driver on the city routes for thirty years.

gaps.prompt: At the primary school, Gran taught ___
gaps.explanation: She wanted to teach art but the school needed a music teacher.

gaps.prompt: Gran's secret of a long marriage: never go to bed ___
gaps.explanation: Grandad’s joke is about fish, but Gran’s real secret is never to go to bed angry.

parts.title: An interview with a woman who found her brother
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Fiona, what did you learn when you were thirty-one?

turns.speaker: fiona
turns.text: My mother wasn’t ill, that’s what I first feared, when she asked me to sit down. And my father didn’t have another family. It was my mother’s secret. She told me that years before I was born she had a baby boy, and she had to give him up for adoption. For thirty years I thought I was her only child.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you start your search?

turns.speaker: fiona
turns.text: I didn’t ask relatives, because my mother wanted it kept private. And the adoption office came later, as I needed his name first. I found a box in the attic with letters that my mother had written in that period, but never sent. They had the hospital, the date and a first name for the baby. That’s where I started.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Why was the search so difficult?

turns.speaker: fiona
turns.text: My mother helped as much as she could. She just didn’t remember much. Money wasn’t a big problem either, the search was free in many places. The real problem was the records. In those years hospitals didn’t write everything down, and papers were lost. Half the pages were missing, and the other half had mistakes.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you finally find him?

turns.speaker: fiona
turns.text: A friend from school offered to ask around, which was kind, but nobody knew. I wrote to a television programme, but they said no. In the end I posted all the details, the date, the hospital and the name, on a website for adopted people. Three months later I got a message from a man: I think I’m your brother.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you feel the first time you spoke?

turns.speaker: fiona
turns.text: I’d been scared for weeks, and I wrote notes on my hand in case I couldn’t speak. I thought I would cry and not say a word. But when he said hello, his voice was so friendly that I felt calmer than I expected. We talked for three hours. He didn’t feel like a stranger at all.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How are things between you now?

turns.speaker: fiona
turns.text: We live four hundred kilometres apart, so we’re not in the same town, and we see each other only twice a year. But we speak on the phone every Sunday, sometimes for an hour. He’s met my children, and he’s like an uncle to them. Next summer, we plan to travel together to the village where he grew up, and I can’t wait.

questions.prompt: What did Fiona learn when she was thirty-one?
options: She had a brother who had been adopted.
Her father had another family elsewhere.
Her mother had been seriously ill for years.
questions.explanation: She was afraid her mother was ill but she was not, and her father had no other family; the secret was a baby boy given up for adoption.

questions.prompt: How did she start her search?
options: By asking her relatives if they knew his name
By visiting the adoption office in person
By reading her mother’s old letters at home
questions.explanation: She did not ask relatives and went to the adoption office later; she began with her mother’s old letters in the attic.

questions.prompt: Why was the search so difficult?
options: Her mother refused to give her any more details.
The records from that time were not complete.
She did not have enough money to keep going.
questions.explanation: Her mother helped and money was not a big problem; hospitals did not write everything down and pages were missing.

questions.prompt: How did she finally find him?
options: Through an old school friend of hers
Through a television programme about families
Through details that were put on a website
questions.explanation: A school friend and a television programme did not help; she posted the details on a website for adopted people.

questions.prompt: How did she feel the first time they spoke?
options: Too nervous to say very much to him
More calm than she had expected
Disappointed that he was a stranger
questions.explanation: She was scared and expected to say nothing, but his friendly voice helped her relax and he did not feel like a stranger.

questions.prompt: How are things between them now?
options: They speak to each other every week.
They live in the same town as each other.
They see each other in person every month.
questions.explanation: They live far apart and meet only twice a year, but they speak on the phone every Sunday.
